summary: LLM inference costs can be reduced by 60-80% through layered optimization techniques including prompt caching, semantic caching, model routing, and output constraints — without sacrificing output quality. Flagship models charge $2-15 per million tokens, making cost optimization critical at production scale; a customer support chatbot handling 1M conversations monthly can cut costs from $3,250/month to under $700 through combined strategies. The highest-leverage techniques are prompt caching (up to 90% off cached input tokens), semantic caching (45% cache hit rates eliminating full round-trips), and intelligent model routing (directing simpler tasks to budget models at 10-20x lower cost).

techniques.name: Prompt Caching
techniques.description: Stores computed key-value tensors for repeated prompt prefixes at the provider level, so subsequent requests reusing the same prefix are charged at a steeply discounted rate (up to 90% off input tokens). Requires structuring prompts so static content (system prompt, knowledge base, instructions) comes first and variable content comes last. Every major provider now supports this natively.
techniques.savings: Up to 90% reduction on cached input tokens; studies show 41-80% overall API cost reduction
techniques.example: Place your 20,000-token RAG knowledge base or detailed system prompt at the top of every request so the prefix stays static across sessions; Anthropic charges only 10% of normal input token cost for cache hits, dropping a $3/M prompt to $0.30/M on repeats.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Caches full LLM responses indexed by semantic similarity of the input query, not exact string match. When a new query is semantically close enough to a cached query (above a configurable similarity threshold), the cached response is returned instantly without calling the LLM at all, eliminating both latency and cost for that request entirely.
techniques.savings: 45% cache hit rate in production deployments; eliminates 100% of token costs for cache hits
techniques.example: Using GPTCache or Redis semantic cache, a customer support bot caches responses to 'How do I reset my password?' so that semantically equivalent queries like 'I forgot my password, what do I do?' return the cached answer instantly at zero token cost.

techniques.name: Model Routing
techniques.description: Classifies incoming requests by complexity and routes them to the cheapest model capable of handling that task. Simple tasks like classification, extraction, summarization, and FAQ answering go to budget models (GPT-4o-mini, Haiku, Gemini Flash), while complex reasoning, coding, or ambiguous multi-step tasks go to frontier models. A thin routing classifier adds minimal latency and cost.
techniques.savings: 50-70% overall cost reduction; routing 70% of traffic to budget models cuts blended cost dramatically
techniques.example: Implement a lightweight classifier that sends classification and extraction tasks to Haiku 4.5 ($1/$5 per M tokens) and reserves Claude Sonnet 4.6 ($3/$15) only for complex reasoning; a real-world split of 70% budget / 25% mid / 5% frontier routinely halves total spend.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Reduces the number of input tokens by trimming verbose instructions, removing redundant few-shot examples, replacing lengthy natural language format instructions with structured schemas, and cutting system prompts to only essential content. Every token removed from a prompt reduces cost linearly with no engineering overhead once templates are optimized.
techniques.example: Audit your system prompt and cut it from 800 tokens to under 200 tokens by replacing verbose role descriptions with concise instructions and swapping five few-shot examples for one clear example with a structured JSON schema — a 30% prompt reduction translates directly to 30% lower input costs.

techniques.name: Output Constraints
techniques.description: Limits the number of output tokens generated by setting max_tokens in API calls, using structured output schemas (JSON mode) instead of verbose prose, and instructing the model to be concise. Output tokens are billed at a 4-5x premium over input tokens on flagship models ($10-15/M vs $2-3/M), making output reduction the highest-dollar-per-token savings opportunity.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens: 256 on a classification endpoint and return structured JSON like {"category": "billing", "confidence": 0.95} instead of a paragraph explanation; this cuts output tokens by 80% on that endpoint, and since output costs 5x more than input, the savings are outsized.

techniques.name: Batch API Processing
techniques.description: Groups multiple non-urgent requests into batch jobs processed asynchronously over a longer window (typically up to 24 hours). Major providers offer 50% discounts on batch API calls versus synchronous requests. Ideal for use cases like bulk document processing, nightly report generation, dataset labeling, and offline evaluations where real-time response is not required.
techniques.savings: 50% reduction on all token costs for batched requests
techniques.example: Run nightly document summarization jobs using Anthropic's Batch API rather than synchronous calls; combined with prompt caching, this stacks to 95% total cost reduction on repeated-prefix batch workloads compared to naive synchronous flagship-model usage.

techniques.name: Context Window Management / Context Trimming
techniques.description: Actively manages what goes into the context window by truncating old conversation turns, summarizing long conversation histories into compressed summaries, and retrieving only the most relevant chunks via RAG rather than stuffing the full knowledge base into every prompt. Long context inputs are expensive because every token in a 100K-token window is billed on every request.
techniques.savings: 30-60% reduction in input costs for conversational or long-context workloads
techniques.example: In a multi-turn chatbot, summarize conversation history older than 10 turns into a 150-token summary rather than passing all prior turns verbatim; on a 50-turn conversation this can reduce context from 8,000 tokens to 1,500 tokens per request, cutting input costs by over 80% for long sessions.

techniques.name: Quantization and Right-Sizing (Self-Hosted)
techniques.description: For teams running their own inference infrastructure, applying quantization (INT8, FP8, GPTQ) to model weights reduces GPU memory requirements, enabling larger batch sizes and cheaper hardware. Right-sizing means choosing the smallest model that meets quality requirements for each task rather than defaulting to the largest available. FP8 on Hopper GPUs is the 2026 gold standard for quality-performance balance.
techniques.savings: 30-75% reduction in self-hosted inference compute costs
techniques.example: Deploy a GPTQ-quantized Llama-3-8B on a single A10G GPU instead of full-precision Llama-3-70B on four A100s for a document classification task; throughput improves and per-request GPU cost drops by over 70% with negligible accuracy degradation on classification benchmarks.

techniques.name: Continuous Batching and KV Cache Reuse (Self-Hosted)
techniques.description: Continuous batching dynamically groups concurrent inference requests at the system level, keeping GPUs saturated rather than processing requests serially. Combined with prefix/KV cache reuse (sharing attention cache across requests with shared prompt prefixes), this can improve throughput by 40-80% and dramatically reduce per-request latency and cost on self-hosted infrastructure.
techniques.savings: 40-80% throughput improvement, translating to 40-80% lower cost per request at scale
techniques.example: Configure vLLM with continuous batching enabled and prefix caching turned on for a coding assistant where all users share a 5,000-token system prompt; the shared prefix is computed once and reused across concurrent requests, delivering up to 23x throughput improvement over naive sequential serving.

techniques.name: Speculative Decoding
techniques.description: Uses a small draft model to speculatively generate multiple candidate tokens that are then verified in parallel by the larger target model. When draft tokens are accepted, the effective tokens-per-second rate of the large model increases significantly, reducing latency and compute cost without changing output quality since the target model's distribution is preserved.
techniques.savings: 20-40% latency reduction; translates to higher throughput and lower cost per token on self-hosted GPU infrastructure
techniques.example: Pair a 7B draft model with a 70B target model in vLLM's speculative decoding mode; for code generation workloads with predictable token patterns, draft acceptance rates of 70-80% are common, effectively delivering 70B quality at closer to 7B serving cost per generated token.

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified Python SDK and proxy server that provides a single OpenAI-compatible interface across 100+ LLM providers. Enables model routing, fallbacks, load balancing, spend tracking, and rate limiting across OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Gemini, Mistral, and self-hosted models. Critical infrastructure for multi-model routing strategies.
tools.pricing_paid: Open source free; LiteLLM Enterprise with advanced features and support available

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching library for LLM applications. Sits in front of any LLM API call, embeds queries, computes similarity against cached responses, and returns cached answers for semantically equivalent questions. Supports multiple vector stores (FAISS, Redis, Milvus) and embedding models.
tools.pricing_paid: Fully open source, no paid tier

tools.name: Redis (Semantic Cache)
tools.description: Redis Stack and Redis Cloud offer a built-in semantic caching layer for LLM responses using vector similarity search. Integrates with LangChain's RedisSemanticCache and can be deployed as middleware in any LLM pipeline to cache and retrieve responses based on query meaning rather than exact match.
tools.pricing_paid: Redis Cloud from $7/month; self-hosted Redis Stack is free

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and cost optimization platform that proxies all API calls to log usage, track per-user and per-feature costs, surface optimization opportunities, and enable caching. Provides dashboards for token spend, latency, error rates, and model comparisons. Essential for understanding where money is actually being spent.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier up to 100K requests/month; Pro from $20/month; Team from $200/month

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: Popular LLM application framework with built-in support for semantic caching (via LLMCache), prompt templating, retrieval-augmented generation, and chain composition. Its caching integrations (InMemoryCache, RedisCache, GPTCache) can be dropped into existing LangChain pipelines with minimal code changes.
tools.pricing_paid: Open source free; LangSmith observability platform from $39/month

tools.name: vLLM
tools.description: High-throughput open-source inference engine for self-hosted LLMs. Implements PagedAttention for efficient KV cache management, continuous batching, prefix caching, speculative decoding, and tensor parallelism. The de-facto standard for production self-hosted LLM serving with up to 23x throughput improvement over naive serving.
tools.pricing_paid: Fully open source; vLLM Enterprise support available via Anyscale

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway and LLMOps platform providing a unified API across providers with built-in semantic caching, automatic model fallbacks, load balancing, request retries, cost tracking, and guardrails. Particularly strong for teams needing production reliability and multi-provider routing without building custom infrastructure.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier available; Growth from $49/month; Enterprise custom pricing

tools.name: Prem AI
tools.description: LLM infrastructure platform focused on cost optimization with built-in prompt compression, semantic caching, model routing, and analytics. Their documented case study achieved 30% token reduction via prompt compression, 45% cache hit rate, and 50% fewer output tokens through a combined optimization strategy deployed in 6 weeks.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier available; paid plans based on usage

tools.name: Maxim AI
tools.description: LLM evaluation and production monitoring platform that includes cost tracking, prompt optimization tooling, and A/B testing for model and prompt variants. Helps identify which prompts and models offer the best quality-to-cost ratio across production traffic.
tools.pricing_paid: Paid plans; pricing available on request

tools.name: OpenMeter
tools.description: Usage metering infrastructure for AI applications that tracks per-user, per-feature, and per-model token consumption in real time. Enables accurate cost allocation, budget enforcement, and identification of high-cost usage patterns to target optimization efforts.
tools.pricing_paid: Open source self-hosted free; Cloud from $0 plus usage

quick_wins: Enable prompt caching immediately by restructuring your prompts so all static content (system prompt, instructions, knowledge base) appears first and variable content last — this alone cuts input token costs by up to 90% on cache hits with zero change to model output quality.

Set max_tokens limits on every API call to prevent runaway responses, and switch format instructions from verbose prose to compact JSON schemas — output tokens cost 4-5x more than input tokens, so even a 30% output reduction has outsized dollar impact.

Audit your system prompt and trim it aggressively to under 200 tokens by removing redundant role-play framing, wordy caveats, and all-but-one few-shot examples — a 30% reduction in prompt length translates directly to 30% lower input costs on every single request.

Route at least your simplest request types (classification, intent detection, entity extraction, FAQ matching) to a budget model like GPT-4o-mini or Haiku 4.5 which cost 10-20x less than frontier models — even routing 50% of traffic to budget models halves your blended per-token cost.

Add a semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis semantic cache via LangChain) in front of your highest-volume endpoints — production deployments consistently see 40-50% cache hit rates, meaning nearly half of all LLM calls are served at zero token cost after the initial population.
